cells.tense: You keep a question genuinely open, and stop when the answer has given what it had.
cells.act: cut through the inertia with one decisive act
cells.ask: When a question has nothing left to give, end it with one plain move — a decision, a walk away, a yes or a no — and treat that move as the finish.
cells.core:
You ask before you believe, and when an answer has given what it had, you set it down and move on lighter. That is rarer than it sounds. Most people either stop asking or keep asking long after the answer has emptied out. You do both halves.

What is still worth practising is the closing move. Catch a question with nothing left to give, tell yourself plainly it is finished, then do one ordinary thing that ends it — not a grand gesture, just the next step. The grip loosens because something else has taken its place. Questions stay clean that way, and so does everything around them.
cells.sheetLine: You ask, and you can set the answer down.
cells.verb: Turns every stone over, with the energy of discovery
cells.place: Clearing space by releasing the grip

cells.tense: You are bracing for an ending that has not arrived, well ahead of where you stand.
cells.act: start something for the spark of starting
cells.ask: Before you decide what to release, begin something small just for the spark of beginning — no destination, no audience, thirty minutes — and count that as the whole of it.
cells.core:
You can feel an ending coming before it is here, and the grip tightens early — not against the ending, but against the not-knowing. The mind starts solving a problem that has not landed, and the release you are practising turns into a rehearsal for something that has not happened.

What resets it is not more discernment. Pick something interesting only because it is new — a notebook, a walk somewhere unfamiliar, a question you cannot answer — and begin it with no plan attached. That fresh start is not a detour from the discipline. It is the ground the discipline stands on when the real ending finally arrives.

cells.tense: You stopped at a moment to let go that had already gone past you.
cells.act: sense what has not happened yet, with wonder
cells.ask: Sit for a minute before you reach for anything today, and sense what hasn't happened yet — no plan, no verdict, just feel toward what's ahead.
cells.core:
The release happened a while back, but you are still on the far side of it, holding what is already gone because finishing it did not finish in you. Or you stopped reaching — the questions got quieter, and you took the quiet as honesty when it was something closing. Either way, the present has gone dim on you.

Do not try to force the interested feeling. Let something catch you instead — a thing you do not understand, a person whose week you do not know the shape of — and stay with that noticing longer than feels useful. Interest is the small entrance this comes back through, and it arrives as curiosity, not as effort.
cells.sheetLine: You let it go already. You're still holding it.

cells.tense: You keep deciding what stays and what goes, without noticing the deciding is yours.
cells.act: make the fair call about a feeling, yourself
cells.ask: Take one feeling that has been waiting on a verdict — the small resentment, the unspoken want — decide what is fair to it, and act on that decision for a week.
cells.core:
You have been running a quiet court for some time — deciding what earns a place in your week, what gets cut, what a feeling is allowed to cost. It runs smoothly. You describe it as just how things work, which is what keeps it invisible even to you. The decisions are being made. The person making them does not appear in the account.

One plain act by your own hand brings that into view. Pick a feeling that has been waiting around for an honest verdict — the small resentment, the unspoken want, the loyalty that has run its course — and settle it yourself, saying so plainly if that helps. You have been keeping this room for a while. Put your name on it.
cells.sheetLine: You have been making this call. Sign it.
